docs.title: Guard Core for EspoCRM
docs.text:
Guard Core for EspoCRM is an EspoCRM extension that adds application-layer security to the EspoCRM API. It is built on psr15-guard and the guard-core-php engine (both MIT).

It screens API requests for attacks, bans clients that misbehave, applies per-route policies and has a passive mode that logs what it would block without blocking anything. It is off until you enable it, and while off it adds one config lookup per request.

The extension registers one global API middleware (globalMiddlewareClassNameList), so it covers public/api/v1/ and the portal API. The guard runs inside the application, so it sees what a perimeter device cannot: the parsed JSON body, the route and the response status. It complements a reverse proxy or WAF, it does not replace one.

This extension holds no security logic. Detection, rate limiting, bans, headers and responses live in the engine. The extension reads the guardCore config, wires the engine to EspoCRM's logger and config, and registers the middleware.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• EspoCRM 9.0.0 or later.
  • PHP 8.2 or later.
  • Redis, optional, for rate limits, behavior rules and bans that hold across requests.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation: the zip, the upload and what uninstalling does.
  • Configuration: the guardCore keys, Redis, trusted proxies.
  • Usage and default policy: what you get with only guardCore.enabled set, and how to roll out from passive mode.
  • Route policies: how routes match, every route option, behavior rules (types, patterns, units, actions).
  • Telemetry agent: the optional agent.
  • What it covers and does not: the entry points and the known limits.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add one key, guardCore, to data/config-internal.php. EspoCRM stores level system config parameters there and rewrites them there on any config save, so a copy kept in data/config.php can end up shadowed or moved. The key is not editable in the admin UI and is never sent to the front end. It is the only root key the extension owns, so nothing collides with other extensions.

'guardCore' => [
    'enabled' => true,
    'enableRedis' => true,
    'redisUrl' => 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379',
    'redisPrefix' => 'espocrm_guard:',
    'trustedProxies' => ['10.0.0.0/8'],
    'routes' => [
        'POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/' => ['rateLimit' => 5, 'rateLimitWindow' => 60],
    ],
],

Clear the cache after changing the config (php command.php clear-cache).

Settings you give override the defaults key by key. A route key is an optional method plus a path, and a null route entry switches a default route off. enabled switches the guard on (the default is off). Every other engine option is a key of guardCore (the named arguments of the engine's SecurityConfig), and every route option a key of a route (RouteConfig). An unknown key or an invalid route option throws instead of being ignored. Options that need a closure or an object (onBlock, authVerifier, customRequestCheck and similar) cannot be expressed in a config file and are rejected.

docs.title: Upgrading from 1.0.0
docs.text:
Version 1.0.0 used two root keys, guardEnabled and guard. Upgrading the extension moves them automatically when they are in data/config.php or data/config-internal.php, which is where the 1.0.0 docs said to put them: the upgrade runs a script that writes guardCore into data/config-internal.php with enabled set from guardEnabled and every setting of guard, then removes the old keys from both files.

  • Old keys in data/config-override.php or data/config-internal-override.php are left alone, because EspoCRM never writes those files. The upgrade changes nothing while either one holds guardEnabled or guard, and the old keys keep working with the deprecation warning until you move them under guardCore yourself.
  • Old keys that you add by hand later still work. The guard logs one deprecation warning when it starts, naming this page.
  • Setting guardCore and one of the old keys at the same time while the guard is on is an error: the middleware throws and says to move everything under guardCore and remove the old keys. When both say the guard is off, nothing happens.
  • If guard is not a map, the upgrade leaves the config as it is, and the middleware reports it loudly when the guard is on.

docs.title: Redis
docs.text: Redis is off by default. Without it, rate limits, behavior rules and bans keep their state per request, so under PHP-FPM they never trigger across requests. Set enableRedis and redisUrl. Only redis://host[:port] is supported: a URL with credentials, a database index or rediss is rejected, because the engine's Redis client connects by host and port only.

docs.title: Trusted proxies and ipAddressServerParam
docs.text: The guard identifies the client by REMOTE_ADDR. EspoCRM's ipAddressServerParam is not read. If you set it to something else (for example HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR), the guard logs a warning, and behind a proxy you must set guardCore.trustedProxies (and guardCore.trustedProxyDepth) so the client is resolved from the forwarded header. Without that every client behind the proxy looks like the proxy.

docs.title: Country filtering
docs.text: The optional ipinfo map (token, and optionally dbPath and maxAge) turns on the IPInfo country database for the engine's country rules.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: guardCore can hold a Redis URL and an agent API key. The extension declares it (and the deprecated guardEnabled and guard) at level system, so EspoCRM never returns them from GET /api/v1/Settings, for any user.

docs.title: What it covers and does not
What it covers
docs.text: The Slim API entry points: public/api/v1/ and the portal API, through the global middleware.

docs.title: What it does not cover
docs.text:
• Non-Slim entry points such as ?entryPoint=... URLs and the OAuth endpoints.
  • Default route keys are literal /api/v1/.... A subdirectory install or portal-specific routes need your own route keys.
  • A honeypot field on the public lead capture form needs a hidden input in the form view. The server side (honeypotFields on the route) works, the client part is not part of this extension.
  • Header exclusion from logs (logSensitiveHeaders) is not in the default policy: guard-core-php 4.4.0 throws a TypeError for a non-empty value. The engine still redacts Authorization, X-Api-Key, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie in its logs.
  • The guard is one layer. It does not replace a reverse proxy, a WAF or EspoCRM's own access control.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download guard-core-<version>.zip from the GitHub release, together with its .sha256 file, or build it (see below).
  2. Check the download with sha256sum -c guard-core-<version>.zip.sha256.
  3. In EspoCRM open Administration > Extensions, upload the zip and click Install.

From the command line the same install is php command.php extension --file=guard-core-<version>.zip, run in the EspoCRM root directory.

Installing changes nothing: guardCore is absent, so the middleware passes every request straight through. See Usage and default policy to turn it on.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Uninstalling removes the middleware and also deletes guardCore (and the old guardEnabled and guard) from the config files. That is on purpose: the extension hides guardCore (it can hold a Redis URL and an agent API key) from the Settings API, and once it is gone nothing would hide those values from logged-in users. Keep a copy of your guardCore block if you plan to reinstall.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: Upgrading from 1.0.0 moves guardEnabled and guard under guardCore automatically. See Configuration.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
npm ci
npm run extension      # builds build/guard-core-<version>.zip

The module bundles only rennf93/psr15-guard and rennf93/guard-core-php. The psr/* packages that psr15-guard requires are provided by EspoCRM itself, so the module composer.json replaces them and none ends up in the package. A size and content check runs in CI on every build.

docs.title: Route policies
docs.text:
A route policy is a set of extra rules for one API path: a rate limit, a ban rule, a size limit, a scan exclusion. You add them under guardCore.routes in data/config-internal.php and clear the cache (php command.php clear-cache).

'guardCore' => [
    'enabled' => true,
    'routes' => [
        'POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/' => ['rateLimit' => 3, 'rateLimitWindow' => 60],
    ],
],

Requests that match no route policy still get everything set at the guardCore level (attack screening, bans, the global rate limit).

docs.title: How a request finds its policy
docs.text:
• A key is an optional HTTP method plus a path: 'POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/' or '/api/v1/'. Without a method the key matches every method.
  • The path matches exactly, or as a prefix when it ends with /. '/api/v1/' matches every API path, 'GET /api/v1/App/user' only that one.
  • The longest matching path wins. On the same path, a key with a method wins over one without.
  • A request gets exactly one route policy. A more specific route replaces the options of a prefix route, it does not add to them. For example the default POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/ route has only a rate limit, so the repeated-401 ban rule of the /api/v1/ route does not apply to lead capture requests. If you want both, put both in the specific route.

docs.title: Default routes
docs.text:
With only guardCore.enabled set, these routes are active:

Route What it does /api/v1/ Bans a client for 1 hour after more than 10 responses with status 401 in 5 minutes on the same path GET /api/v1/App/user The same ban rule (this is the login call) POST /api/v1/Attachment/chunk/ No body scan (file chunks), plus the same ban rule POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/ At most 10 requests per minute per client POST /api/v1/User/passwordChangeRequest At most 5 requests per 5 minutes per client POST /api/v1/User/changePasswordByRequest At most 5 requests per 5 minutes per client

docs.title: Changing or switching off a default route
docs.text:
• A route you set with the same key as a default route replaces it as a whole. Options of the default route that you leave out are gone, so repeat the ones you want to keep.
  • A route set to null switches the default route off: the extension removes it, and requests to that path fall back to the next matching route, usually /api/v1/.
'guardCore' => [
    'enabled' => true,
    'routes' => [
        // Lead capture: 3 requests per minute instead of 10.
        'POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/' => ['rateLimit' => 3, 'rateLimitWindow' => 60],
        // No more 5 per 5 minutes limit on password reset requests.
        // The path now falls back to the /api/v1/ route (only the 401 ban rule).
        'POST /api/v1/User/passwordChangeRequest' => null,
    ],
],

docs.title: Behavior rules
docs.text:
A behavior rule counts what one client does on one path and acts when the count goes over a threshold.

'GET /api/v1/App/user' => ['behaviorRules' => [[
    'rule_type' => 'return_pattern', // count responses that match the pattern
    'pattern' => 'status:401',       // responses with status 401
    'threshold' => 3,                // act when the count goes above 3 (on the 4th)
    'window' => 300,                 // within the last 300 seconds
    'action' => 'ban',               // ban the client's IP
    'ban_duration' => 3600,          // for 3600 seconds
]]],
Key Values Default rule_type return_pattern: counts responses to the client that match pattern. usage and frequency: count the client's requests to the path (both behave the same in this version) required threshold Whole number, 1 or more. The action runs when the count goes above it required window Seconds, a sliding window. 0 means the default 3600 pattern Only for return_pattern, see below none action ban, log, alert or throttle, see below log ban_duration Seconds the ban lasts, for action ban 3600

Patterns for return_pattern:

Pattern Matches status:401 Responses with that status code. Any code works: status:403, status:404 (404 scanning), status:429 json:path.to.field==value A JSON response whose field equals the value, case insensitive. A last segment ending in [] matches any element of an array: json:tags[]==admin regex:... A response body that matches the regular expression, case insensitive any other text A response body that contains the text, case insensitive

Only status: patterns work out of the box. The other three read the response body, so they need 'behaviorScanResponseBody' => true at the guardCore level; without it a route rule with such a pattern never matches. The body is read up to 262144 bytes (behaviorMaxResponseBodyInspectBytes).

Actions:

Action What happens ban The client's IP is banned for ban_duration seconds. Every API request from it then gets a 403, on every route (unless a route sets 'bypassedChecks' => ['ip_ban']) log A warning line in data/logs alert A critical line in data/logs throttle In the engine version this extension ships (guard-core-php 4.4.0) it only writes a log line. It does not slow down or block the client

Things to know:

  • Counts are kept per client IP and per method plus exact path, not per route key. The /api/v1/ default rule counts the 401 responses of each path separately.
  • The rule acts after the request that crosses the threshold is answered: that request goes through, the ban applies from the next one.
  • In passive mode (the default) nothing is banned. You get a [PASSIVE MODE] Would ban IP ... line instead.
  • Without Redis the counts start from zero on every request under PHP-FPM, so a rule never fires. Set enableRedis and redisUrl (see Configuration).
  • correlate_with_detection is accepted but only changes global rules (globalBehaviorRules at the guardCore level), not route rules.

docs.title: All route options
docs.text: Every key below goes inside a route, next to behaviorRules. An unknown key makes the extension throw when it builds the guard, so a typo in a key name shows up as an error, not as a silent no-op. The status codes are what the client gets with 'passiveMode' => false; in passive mode the request passes and the would-be block is logged.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Option Example What it does rateLimit 10 At most this many requests per client IP on this path per window, then 429. The global limit still applies too rateLimitWindow 60 The window for rateLimit, in seconds. Default 60 geoRateLimits ['DE' => ['limit' => 20, 'window' => 60], '*' => ['limit' => 5, 'window' => 60]] A limit per client country, * for every other country. Window in seconds. Needs ipinfo, without it the whole option is skipped maxRequestSize 1048576 Bytes. A larger Content-Length gets 413. A request without Content-Length (chunked) is not checked allowedContentTypes ['application/json'] Any other Content-Type gets 415. Lowercase, exact match, parameters such as ; charset=utf-8 are ignored. A request with no Content-Type (a GET) is rejected too, so use it on POST-only routes

rateLimit and geoRateLimits need Redis to count across requests (see Configuration).

docs.title: Who can call the route
docs.text:
Option Example What it does ipWhitelist ['203.0.113.7', '10.0.0.0/8'] Only these IPs or CIDR ranges, everyone else gets 403. When set, ipBlacklist and the global IP lists are ignored on this route ipBlacklist ['198.51.100.0/24'] These IPs or ranges get 403 blockedCountries ['CN', 'RU'] Uppercase ISO codes get 403. Needs ipinfo, without it nobody is blocked whitelistCountries ['IT', 'DE'] Only these countries, everyone else gets 403. Needs ipinfo, without it every request is blocked blockCloudProviders ['AWS', 'GCP', 'Azure:!eastus'] Requests from the published ranges of AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean, Linode or Vultr get 403. Provider:!region leaves one region out. Names are case sensitive blockedUserAgents ['sqlmap', 'python-requests'] A User-Agent that matches one of these regular expressions (case insensitive, anywhere in the text) gets 403. Adds to the global list timeRestrictions ['start' => '09:00', 'end' => '18:00', 'timezone' => 'Europe/Rome'] Outside the window, 403. 24 hour HH:MM with leading zeros, timezone optional (default UTC). A start after the end is an overnight window requireReferrer ['example.com'] A request without Referer or with a Referer from another domain gets 403. Subdomains count requireHttps true A plain HTTP request gets a 301 to the https URL. Behind a TLS proxy set trustXForwardedProto and trustedProxies at the guardCore level, or every request looks like HTTP

Client IPs come from REMOTE_ADDR unless trustedProxies is set (see Configuration).

docs.title: What the request must carry
docs.text:
Option Example What it does requiredHeaders ['X-Requested-With' => 'XMLHttpRequest', 'X-Client' => 'required'] A map of header to value. A missing header or a different value gets 400. The value required means any value. A plain list (['X-Client']) does not work authorizationHeaderRequired 'bearer' The Authorization header must be there with that scheme (bearer or basic), else 401. It checks that a token is sent, not that it is valid: EspoCRM does that honeypotFields ['website'] A POST, PUT or PATCH with a JSON or form body where one of these top-level fields is filled gets 403. The field has to exist in your form and stay empty for people

authRequired, apiKeyRequired and apiKeyHeader are accepted but do not work in this extension: they call a verifier function, which a config file cannot hold, so every request on the route fails with 401. Use authorizationHeaderRequired.

docs.title: Attack screening on the route
docs.text:
Option Example What it does enableSuspiciousDetection false Turns attack screening off for this route. Default true detectionScanBody false Screens the path, query and headers but not the body. The default POST /api/v1/Attachment/chunk/ route uses it enabledDetectionCategories ['sqli', 'xss'] Only these categories on this route, [] for none. Names: xss, sqli, dir_traversal, path_traversal, cmd_injection, file_inclusion, ldap, xml, ssrf, nosql, file_upload, template, http_split, sensitive_file, cms_probing, recon, proto_pollution, code_injection, deserialization. A misspelled name is not rejected here, it just never matches excludedDetectionParams ['q'] Query parameters left out of the screening. Lowercase. Replaces the global list on this route excludedDetectionBodyFields ['description'] Body fields left out of the screening, at any depth of a JSON body. Lowercase. Replaces the global list on this route excludedDetectionHeaders ['x-forwarded-host'] Headers still screened, but an address in them (a host or IP list) is not taken for SSRF. Adds to the built-in list excludedSemanticDetectionHeaders ['x-client-note'] Headers kept out of the semantic analysis only, the pattern screening still runs. Adds to the global list

A detected attack gets 400.

docs.title: Skipping checks
docs.text: Option Example What it does bypassedChecks ['rate_limit'] Skips engine checks on this route: ip_ban, ip (IP and country lists), clouds, rate_limit, penetration (attack screening), or all for those five. It does not skip the other options on this page

docs.title: Telemetry agent
docs.text:
The guard-agent-php agent is optional and is not bundled. To use it, run in the EspoCRM root directory:

composer require rennf93/guard-agent-php

then add an agent map to guardCore:

'guardCore' => [
    'enabled' => true,
    'agent' => ['apiKey' => 'your-project-api-key'],
],

The extension loads the agent only when the package is present, and fails with a clear message when agent is configured without it. When an agent is configured, enableAgent defaults to true. The agent is started with the first guarded request and flushes its buffer when the request ends.

An EspoCRM upgrade replaces vendor/, so run the composer require command again after upgrading.

The agent API key lives in guardCore, which is hidden from the Settings API.

docs.title: Usage and default policy
docs.text:
With only 'enabled' => true under guardCore you get the default policy:

  • Passive mode: what would be blocked is logged, nothing is blocked.
  • Attack screening of paths, query strings, headers and JSON or form bodies is on.
  • No body scan on POST /api/v1/Attachment/chunk/.
  • A ban rule after more than 10 responses with status 401 in 5 minutes on GET /api/v1/App/user and on every other API path (counted per path).
  • Rate limits on POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/ (10 per minute) and on the two password routes (5 per 5 minutes).

docs.title: Rolling out
docs.text:
1. Set 'guardCore' => ['enabled' => true] and clear the cache.
  2. Watch data/logs for Guard would block by ... lines. Each line names the check, the reason and the client, and the request still passes.
  3. Fix or exclude what is a false positive, for example with a route policy.
  4. Set 'passiveMode' => false. Blocked requests now log Guard blocked by ... and get the engine's response (400 for a detected attack, 403 for a banned client, 429 for a rate limit).

Redis matters for steps 3 and 4: without it the rate limits and bans do not hold across requests.

docs.title: Route policies
docs.text:
Route policies explains how a request finds its route, what switching a default route off does, and every option and behavior rule key with its unit.

'guardCore' => [
    'enabled' => true,
    'routes' => [
        // A stricter lead capture limit.
        'POST /api/v1/LeadCapture/' => ['rateLimit' => 3, 'rateLimitWindow' => 60],
        // Switch a default route off.
        'POST /api/v1/User/passwordChangeRequest' => null,
        // A ban after repeated 401 responses.
        'GET /api/v1/App/user' => ['behaviorRules' => [[
            'rule_type' => 'return_pattern',
            'pattern' => 'status:401',
            'threshold' => 3,
            'window' => 300,
            'action' => 'ban',
            'ban_duration' => 3600,
        ]]],
    ],
],

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: examples/simple_app runs a real EspoCRM with MariaDB and the default policy. examples/advanced_app adds Redis, an nginx reverse proxy with trustedProxies, passive mode off and the route policies above. Both install the built extension zip through EspoCRM's own extension install, and both are exercised by the Live Smoke workflow.
